dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Loo-da-lay, hip-hip hooray, I'm officially in love with the great outdoors... What a great place this is...

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Just look at this place — nothing but rocks and animals. Not a bearing in sight.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: *sigh* If I'd known it'd be like this, I would have invited my suppliers along, too...

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Never mind, whatever, I'll just keep reading this scripture...

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Vernadska... Vernadska, what did she do wrong? What could she do wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know her?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: No, no. Not in the least. Well, not in the sense that "know" might imply some sort of two-way familiarity.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: It might be more accurate to say I "know of" her, though I doubt she's even aware of me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: See you later. Now, where did that wrench get to...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you "know of" her?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: I've seen her a couple of times while making jumping frogs for the children.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: I'm positively certain that she's not a bad person.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Is that it?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: That's it. I trust my instincts.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: ...What could Vernadska have done wrong that the Moonchanter would punish her personally?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: How could anyone do anything wrong in a place this empty? I need to go into town to buy materials just to build a basic water pump.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: *sigh* But if she must be punished, then she must be punished. And it has to be said, Miss Lauma is far kinder than my old boss...

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Geez, memorizing these prayers is a tough ask. Might as well read a manual...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you... a member of the Frostmoon Scions?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Nope. Not before, and not now. In the future... Maybe. Maybe not.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: #Still, I have heard of you, {NICKNAME}. You're quite famous around these parts.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Pleased to meet you either way. I'm Mirsky, a machinist from Nasha Town. As to why I'm learning all this... Well, it's for love.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, the Scions' teachings are rather tiring material.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: I had great faith in my memory, but...

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: I must admit that I'd rather memorize the operating rules for some messier machines than do the same for these doctrines.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: At the very least, operating instructions can be verified...

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: *cough* A—Actually, ah, never mind. I never said any of that. And if anyone asks, you didn't hear anything either, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And who is this dearly beloved of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Uh... Yeah. Don't ask. I can't tell you either, or I'll cause her trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just a name? Trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: O—Of course... Come on, what's with that look? I haven't done anything wrong, and neither would she.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: We both love tinkering with machines, so we sometimes meet to exchange pointers and further our knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: I mean, just look around us. What could we build here? Not even an automatic water pump, I'd say.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: At the most, we might grab some scrap with which to build some jumping toy frog. *sigh* I could do so much more if only Miss Lauma would provide more funding...

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alright, alright. Enough yammering for now. I've prayers to memorize.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Once I do, maybe she and I can pray together as well.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Wait, no, this line is... *sigh* Come on, Mirsky. Stop thinking about the materials. But... will Miss Lauma really agree to...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Perhaps Lauma can help him out...)

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: (Mirsky runs his hands through his hair in frustration over a certain... or perhaps a certain number of things...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It seems that he'd like to speak to Lauma...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Perhaps <color=#FFCC33FF>Lauma</color> can help him with his troubles...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Wait, no, this line is... *sigh* Come on, Mirsky. Stop thinking about the materials. But... will Miss Lauma really agree to...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hello there, Mr. Mirsky.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Oh, Miss Lauma, you're here. What do you think of my previous suggestion?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: I just need some simple materials, and I'll be able to give this place a facelift.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Automatic water pump, support rods to reinforce houses, and sewing machines... You name them, I can make them.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Any scrap left over, I can make into small jumping frogs for the kids. They love toys like that.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Well, if you're willing to help, that would be great. We will pay you the relevant fees, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Pay? Ah, right. Thank you for your generosity. But what I'm more concerned with is... Would you be willing to let me into the library to peruse the books?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: I believe the information on kuuvahki that I wish to find can be found in there.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You are our guest. Naturally, the library gates are always open to you.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, I mean, can I borrow it and read it somewhere else, or maybe make a copy...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'm afraid not. Those books can only be read within library premises.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Alright, that's more than enough. I'll head there once I'm done packing.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You're always welcome... Oh, and one more thing. Should you see an acolyte busy copying doctrinal text in the library, please refrain from disturbing her.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: She made a mistake, and has just finished her meditation. She now has to copy doctrinal texts until she can realign her thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Copying those texts? Heh. You're a kind soul, Miss Lauma. If I'd made a mistake under my old boss's watch, I'd have wound up owing him more Mora than I could make in this life or the next.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Well, I would say that it is a severe enough punishment for Vernadska.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Perhaps, but for me, copying text is...

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: W—Wait. What? Who did you say was being punished again?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Vernadska. Are you two acquainted?

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Err... No! I—It's just... This name feels familiar somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: If you'll allow me, might I ask when Miss Vernadska will be busy with her copying? It is official business, after all, and I'd rather not disturb her in any way.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Every day. But there's no need to walk on eggshells. She will be doing her work at a separate location. So long as you exercise a little more care, you won't disturb her.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsky
dialogues.text: Alright, I see. Uh... I'll pack up and head to the library right away, if you don't mind.
